Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows lucent streaks of air outlining the mediastinal structures, particularly along the left heart border and extending into the neck (continuous diaphragm sign), which is characteristic of spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect). Esophageal rupture typically presents with more severe systemic symptoms and often pleural effusion, while the distribution here fits the classic anterior/upper mediastinal pattern of air tracking from ruptured alveoli.
